description: Anchored PQ-key binding — the verifier RE-DERIVES the binding's content-address from raw bytes; the key manifest is discovery only. canonical_content = JCS(statement); canonical_content_sha256 = sha256(canonical_content). For a NIP-01 carrier also: event_id = sha256(compact-JSON [0,pubkey,created_at,kind,tags,content]). DUAL-ALGORITHM CONVERGENCE: vector 1 (invinoveritas) uses ML-DSA-65 (lattice) with a Nostr carrier; vector 2 (KYA-L4) uses SLH-DSA-SHA2-192s (hash-based) anchored on-chain via OCP — two independent NIST-PQC families reproducing byte-compatible content-addresses under ONE profile via the same JCS canon, proving {algorithm} is a field, not a fork. Signature checks (BIP-340 / ML-DSA / SLH-DSA) are the separate deep lane; this suite pins the self-verifying content-address both must sign.

vectors.name: invinoveritas-pq-key-binding-v1-live
vectors.note: Fede's FIRST REAL live binding (api.babyblueviper.com/.well-known/pq-key-binding.json): binds the pinned invinoveritas verifier secp256k1 key 6786e18a… to an ML-DSA-65 (FIPS-204) PQ key, OTS-anchored to Bitcoin. Independently recomputed byte-exact.

vectors.name: kya-l4-pq-key-binding-v0-slh-dsa
vectors.note: KYA-L4 PRODUCTION binding (SLH-DSA-SHA2-192s, SPHINCS+, NIST level 3 to match ML-DSA-65): binds the 0xFf9a…ca14 classical identity to a hash-based PQ key, OCP-anchored on Ethereum MAINNET — record(bytes32) of this content-address at TruthAnchor 0x1e2A118a2bf1C240aE6fDe187c07f905D360f094, tx 0x469655a08accf0300def211bf0c9ebd463e65b89f4ede1ac372ed2796e7ba916 (block 25646404). The anchor tx is sent BY 0xFf9a, so it doubles as the classical proof-of-possession; the SLH-DSA companion signs the content-address (sig 16224 B). No NIP-01 carrier. Served live + recomputed in-browser at ai.verticecriativo.pt/quantum. Same JCS canon as vector 1 → byte-compatible content-address, different NIST-PQC family.

vectors.name: kya-l4-pq-key-binding-v0-rotation-1-slh-dsa
vectors.note: ROTATION binding #1 (#133): same classical identity 0xFf9a, NEW SLH-DSA key 8488157a…, links predecessor via predecessor_content_address = vector 2's cc b26a0159…. Dual-signed over its own content-address by the PREDECESSOR PQ key (continuity — the old key authorizes the rotation, so it survives the classical break) AND by the new key (possession); both signatures + the served artifact live in pq-key-binding-v0.rotation.json (deep lane, SLH-DSA verify in-browser). Here the hash lane pins the content-address the chain resolves over; the in-force resolution across {vector2, this} is exercised in pq-key-binding-v0.rotation-vectors.json via cutoff_enforce.py.

vectors.name: kya-example-binding-v0-slh-dsa
vectors.note: A DEDICATED example binding (SLH-DSA key 0b15e3ba…) used only to demonstrate the revocation lane (#134), so the production genesis/rotation chain is untouched. Content-address recomputes here; it is the target of the revocation in the next vector.

vectors.name: kya-key-revocation-v0-of-example
vectors.note: A REVOCATION statement — its own class (schema kya.pq_key_revocation.v0), NOT a binding: it names the binding it revokes by content-address (964af387… above) and is PQ-authorized by that binding's key (pq_key_revocation.v0, signature in pq-key-binding-v0.revocation.json). It carries NO trusted revoked_at — a revocation takes effect at ITS OWN anchor time (never a self-declared field). The hash lane pins its content-address; the temporal rule is exercised in pq-key-binding-v0.revocation-vectors.json.
